content:
### Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

> **Category:** DoJ Overview & Administrative Structure > **Source URL:** https://doj.gov.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate
metadata.sectionTitle: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

content:
### 1. Overview and Constitutional Mandate

The Department of Justice (DoJ) is part of the Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of India. It performs administrative, advisory, and developmental functions related to the administration of justice in India in accordance with the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961. The DoJ acts as an institutional bridge between the Union Executive and the Judiciary, respecting the constitutional independence of the higher judiciary while facilitating budgetary, technological, and infrastructural assistance. ---

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

content:
### A. Appointment Division (Judicial Appointments)

- Facilitates the appointment and conditions of service of the Chief Justice of India, Judges of the Supreme Court of India, Chief Justices, and Judges of all 25 High Courts in India. - Coordinates the constitutional collegium process under Articles 124, 217, and 224 of the Constitution of India. - Handles matters relating to the resignation, retirement, salaries, pensions, and leave rules of higher judiciary judges.

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

content:
### B. eCourts Project Division (ICT & Modernization)

- Formulates, monitors, and implements the flagship eCourts Mission Mode Project in partnership with the eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India. - Oversees computerization, cloud infrastructure, video-conferencing facilities, and digital connectivity (WAN/LAN) across thousands of district and subordinate court complexes. - Manages key public portals: eCourts Services, National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), eFiling, ePay, and Virtual Courts.

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

sectionTitle: C. Access to Justice (A2J) & Legal Aid Division
content:
### C. Access to Justice (A2J) & Legal Aid Division

- Implements policies and schemes to enhance access to justice for poor, marginalized, vulnerable groups, women, children, and undertrial prisoners. - Operates the **DISHA Scheme** (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice in India), integrating Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu (pro bono legal services), and Nyaya Mitra initiatives. - Coordinates with the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs).

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate
metadata.sectionTitle: C. Access to Justice (A2J) & Legal Aid Division

content:
### D. Judicial Infrastructure Division

- Administers the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the Judiciary. - Provides central funding assistance to State Governments and Union Territories for constructing court halls, residential accommodations for judicial officers, digital litigant waiting rooms, and vulnerable witness rooms.

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate

sectionTitle: E. Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) Division
content:
### E. Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) Division

- Monitors and supports the implementation of Fast Track Special Courts across States and UTs dedicated to the expeditious trial of cases under the POCSO Act and rape offences. ---

metadata.title: Department of Justice: Divisions, Functions, and Mandate
metadata.sectionTitle: E. Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) Division

- **Official Website:** [https://doj.gov.in](https://doj.gov.in) - **Ministry:** Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of India, Jaisalmer House, 26, Man Singh Road, New Delhi - 110011.

### Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

> **Category:** Fast-Track Justice & POCSO Cases > **Source URL:** https://doj.gov.in/fast-track-special-courts/ > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

content:
### 1. Background and Legislative Mandate

In the aftermath of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, which introduced stringent penalties for sexual offences against children and women, the Union Cabinet approved a Centrally Sponsored Scheme to set up **Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)** across the nation. The scheme is administered by the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, in coordination with State Governments and High Courts, funded partly through the **Nirbhaya Fund**. ---

metadata.title: Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

content:
### 2. Core Objectives

- Expeditious trial and disposal of pending rape cases under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (now corresponding sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita). - Dedicated adjudication of offences under the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012**. - Minimizing victim trauma through child-friendly courtrooms, vulnerable witness deposition complexes, and swift disposal within statutory timelines. ---

metadata.title: Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

content:
### 3. Implementation and Operational Scale

- **Approved Target:** Setup of 1,023 Fast Track Special Courts across India, including 389 exclusive POCSO Courts. - **Current Operational Courts:** Over 750+ FTSCs actively functioning across participating States and Union Territories (as per latest Department of Justice progress reports). - **Specialized Features:** - Dedicated Special Judges and Special Public Prosecutors. - Video-recorded testimony facilities to shield child victims from the accused. - Periodic case monitoring directly mapped on the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG). ---

metadata.title: Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

sectionTitle: 4. How Citizens and Litigants Can Access Information
content:
### 4. How Citizens and Litigants Can Access Information

- Victims and families can contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or Protection Officers under the POCSO Act. - Case tracking for cases assigned to FTSCs can be done on the eCourts Services portal and mobile app using the unique 16-digit CNR number. - Official scheme performance reports are updated at [https://doj.gov.in/fast-track-special-courts/](https://doj.gov.in/fast-track-special-courts/).

metadata.title: Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)

sectionTitle: 1. Supreme Court of India: Sanctioned Strength and Appointment
content:
### 1. Supreme Court of India: Sanctioned Strength and Appointment

- **Sanctioned Strength:** 34 Judges (including the Chief Justice of India) pursuant to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019. - **Constitutional Basis:** Appointments are made by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution based on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium. - **Retirement Age:** 65 years. ---

metadata.title: Judges Strength, Appointment Process, and Vacancy Data
metadata.status: Verified Official Government Data (Figures represent baseline official statistics; subject to dynamic updates)
metadata.sectionTitle: 1. Supreme Court of India: Sanctioned Strength and Appointment

content:
### 2. High Courts: Structure and Vacancies

- India currently has **25 High Courts** serving States and Union Territories. - **Total Approved Strength:** 1,114 Judges across all 25 High Courts (Permanent + Additional Judges). - **Appointment Procedure:** - Governed by the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) framed pursuant to the Three Judges Cases. - High Court Collegium recommends names to the Chief Minister / Governor, Union Minister of Law & Justice, and the Supreme Court Collegium. - Warrants of appointment are issued by the President of India under Article 217 / 224. - **Retirement Age:** 62 years. - **Vacancy Dynamics:** Vacancies fluctuate continuously due to retirements, resignations, elevations, and new appointment notifications published in the Gazette of India by the Department of Justice. ---

metadata.title: Judges Strength, Appointment Process, and Vacancy Data
metadata.status: Verified Official Government Data (Figures represent baseline official statistics; subject to dynamic updates)

content:
### 3. District and Subordinate Judiciary

- **Administrative Jurisdiction:** The recruitment, promotion, and service conditions of District and Subordinate Judges fall under the administrative jurisdiction of the respective High Courts and State Governments under Articles 233, 234, and 235 of the Constitution. - **Sanctioned vs Working Strength (Approximate National Benchmark):** - Approved Strength: ~25,000 judicial officers nationwide. - Working Strength: ~19,000 to ~20,000 judicial officers. - Ongoing recruitments are conducted through State Judicial Services Examinations. ---

sectionTitle: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
content:
### Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative

Category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid Source URL: https://doj.gov.in/nyaya-bandhu/ Retrieval Date: 2026-11-11 Verification Status: Verified Official Government Data

metadata.title: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
metadata.category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid
metadata.sectionTitle: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative

content:
### OVERVIEW

Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) is an initiative of the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India. The primary objective is to encourage advocates across the nation to offer pro bono legal counsel to disadvantaged individuals and marginalized communities who cannot afford legal representation.

metadata.title: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
metadata.category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid

content:
### KEY OBJECTIVES

1. Foster a culture of pro bono legal culture in India among practicing advocates and law students. 2. Provide free, high-quality legal representation to marginalized litigants before High Courts and Subordinate Courts. 3. Leverage mobile technology to connect registered pro bono advocates directly with eligible applicants through the Nyaya Bandhu Mobile App.

metadata.title: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
metadata.category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid

content:
### ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

Beneficiaries eligible under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 can apply for assistance, including: - Women and children - Members of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) - Victims of human trafficking - Persons with disabilities - Victims of mass disasters, ethnic violence, or caste atrocities - Low-income citizens whose annual income falls below state-prescribed thresholds

metadata.title: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
metadata.category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid

content:
### APPLICATION PROCEDURE

1. Litigants download the Nyaya Bandhu Mobile Application (Android/iOS) or register on https://www.probono-doj.in. 2. Submit identity proof, income certificate or caste certificate establishing eligibility under Section 12. 3. Provide case filing details and select the court establishment. 4. The application is reviewed and assigned to an enrolled volunteer advocate who agrees to handle the matter pro bono.

metadata.title: Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono Legal Services) Initiative
metadata.category: Pro Bono Legal Services & Legal Aid

sectionTitle: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
content:
### Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized

> **Category:** Access to Justice & Free Legal Services > **Source URL:** https://doj.gov.in/tele-law/ > **Dedicated Portal:** https://www.tele-law.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
metadata.category: Access to Justice & Free Legal Services
metadata.sectionTitle: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized

content:
### 1. What is Tele-Law?

Tele-Law is an innovative flagship program under the **DISHA Scheme** of the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, launched in 2017 in partnership with the Common Services Centres (CSC) e-Governance Services India Limited and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). It connects marginalized, disadvantaged, and remote citizens directly with Panel Lawyers stationed at State Legal Services Authorities through video-conferencing, audio-calling, and the Tele-Law Mobile App. ---

metadata.title: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
metadata.category: Access to Justice & Free Legal Services

sectionTitle: 2. Who is Entitled to Free Legal Advice?
content:
### 2. Who is Entitled to Free Legal Advice?

Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, the following categories receive **100% free legal advice**: - Women and children. - Members of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). - Victims of human trafficking or beggar systems. - Persons with disabilities / differently-abled persons. - Victims of mass disasters, ethnic violence, caste atrocities, flood, drought, earthquake, or industrial disaster. - Industrial workers. - Persons in custody or in protective homes / juvenile facilities. - Low-income citizens (annual income thresholds prescribed by respective State Governments). - Other citizens can access the service for a nominal fee fixed by CSC guidelines. ---

metadata.title: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
metadata.category: Access to Justice & Free Legal Services
metadata.sectionTitle: 2. Who is Entitled to Free Legal Advice?

sectionTitle: Method A: Through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLE) at Common Service Centres (CSCs)
content:
### Method A: Through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLE) at Common Service Centres (CSCs)

1. Citizen visits their nearest village CSC kiosk. 2. The Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE) or Para-Legal Volunteer (PLV) enters citizen details and brief case nature on the Tele-Law portal. 3. An appointment slot is scheduled with a Panel Lawyer. 4. On the scheduled appointment, the citizen speaks with the lawyer via secure video conference or phone call. 5. The lawyer provides professional, pre-litigation legal advice, explaining next steps, document requirements, and whether legal representation via Legal Services Clinics or DLSA is required.

metadata.title: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
metadata.category: Access to Justice & Free Legal Services
metadata.sectionTitle: Method A: Through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLE) at Common Service Centres (CSCs)

sectionTitle: Method B: Tele-Law Citizen Mobile Application
content:
### Method B: Tele-Law Citizen Mobile Application

- Available for direct download on Android Google Play Store and iOS App Store. - Allows direct self-registration, appointment booking, document attachment, and consultation without visiting a physical center. ---

metadata.title: Tele-Law Service: Mainstreaming Legal Aid to the Marginalized
metadata.category: Access to Justice & Free Legal Services
metadata.sectionTitle: Method B: Tele-Law Citizen Mobile Application

content:
### 4. Key Metrics and Milestone Achievements

- Tele-Law is operational in all 36 States and Union Territories. - Integrated across more than 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats and Common Service Centres nationwide. - Over 60 lakh+ pre-litigation legal consultations facilitated since inception. - Toll-free grievance helpline and support available via the official portal. ---

- **Tele-Law Web Portal:** [https://www.tele-law.in](https://www.tele-law.in) - **DoJ Scheme Page:** [https://doj.gov.in/tele-law/](https://doj.gov.in/tele-law/)

sectionTitle: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup
content:
### Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup

> **Category:** Case Status Verification & Citizen Services > **Source URL:** https://services.ecourts.gov.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup
metadata.sectionTitle: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup

content:
### 1. What is a CNR Number?

The **Case Number Record (CNR)** is a unique 16-character alphanumeric code assigned to every single case filed across any District or Subordinate Court in India. Format: `XXXX01-000123-2024` - Characters 1-2: State Code (e.g., DL for Delhi, MH for Maharashtra) - Characters 3-4: District Code - Characters 5-6: Court Complex Code - Characters 7-12: Sequential Case Filing Serial Number - Characters 13-16: Year of Filing Because the CNR is globally unique, entering the CNR directly retrieves the complete case dossier without needing to choose state, district, or court name. ---

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup

content:
### Method A: By 16-Digit CNR Number (Fastest)

1. Open [https://services.ecourts.gov.in](https://services.ecourts.gov.in) or open the **eCourts Services Mobile App**. 2. Tap or click on **CNR Number Search**. 3. Enter your 16-digit CNR without hyphens or spaces. 4. Complete the security captcha. 5. Click **Search**. 6. The screen presents: - Case Details (Filing Date, Registration Number, Case Type) - Case Status (First Hearing Date, Next Hearing Date, Stage of Case, Court Number & Presiding Judge) - Petitioner and Respondent Names - Advocates appearing - Complete History of Case Hearings (Daily Business, Orders, and interim Judgments available as downloadable PDF).

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup

sectionTitle: Method B: Case Number Search (When CNR is not known)
content:
### Method B: Case Number Search (When CNR is not known)

1. Select State, District, and Court Complex. 2. Select Case Type from the dropdown list. 3. Enter Case Number and Year of Filing. 4. Click Search.

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup
metadata.sectionTitle: Method B: Case Number Search (When CNR is not known)

sectionTitle: Method C: Party Name / FIR Search
content:
### Method C: Party Name / FIR Search

- Litigants can search using their own name or respondent's name. - In criminal cases, search by entering the Police Station name, FIR Number, and Year. ---

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup
metadata.sectionTitle: Method C: Party Name / FIR Search

content:
### 3. Important Citizen Advisory

- **Antigravity / JusticeAI Chatbot Limitation:** Third-party AI chatbots do not possess direct API write access or real-time live judicial docket databases. - For official certified case status, summons, or warrants, citizens must always inspect [https://services.ecourts.gov.in](https://services.ecourts.gov.in) or the eCourts mobile app.

metadata.title: Citizen Guide: Current Case Status and CNR Number Lookup

sectionTitle: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal
content:
### eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal

> **Category:** Digital Citizen Services & Case Tracking > **Source URL:** https://ecourts.gov.in > **Secondary Portal:** https://services.ecourts.gov.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal
metadata.sectionTitle: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal

sectionTitle: 1. What is the eCourts Services Project?
content:
### 1. What is the eCourts Services Project?

The eCourts Mission Mode Project is a Pan-India project conceptualized under the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) and monitored by the eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India in collaboration with the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, and the National Informatics Centre (NIC). The project empowers litigants, advocates, law enforcement agencies, and the public with 24x7 online access to judicial services without requiring physical visits to court premises. ---

metadata.title: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal
metadata.sectionTitle: 1. What is the eCourts Services Project?

sectionTitle: 2. Features of the eCourts Services Mobile Application
content:
### 2. Features of the eCourts Services Mobile Application

The **eCourts Services Mobile App** is the official citizen-facing mobile application available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store. Key Features: 1. **CNR Number Search:** Search any case anywhere in India using the unique 16-character alphanumeric Case Number Record (CNR). 2. **Multi-Parameter Search:** - Case Type and Case Number - Filing Number - Party Name (Petitioner / Respondent) - Advocate Name / Bar Registration Number - FIR Number (Police Station, Year, and FIR No.) - Act & Section 3. **QR Code Scanning:** Every certified copy and court order generated via CIS (Case Information System) carries an encrypted QR code that can be scanned using the in-app scanner to fetch instant verified case history. 4. **Cause List Generation:** Advocates and litigants can view daily, weekly, and custom court cause lists for any court hall. 5. **My Cases Portfolio:** Save tracked cases to an automated personal diary with push notifications for next hearing dates, interim orders, and final disposal judgments. 6. **Bilingual & Multi-Language Support:** Available in English, Hindi, and various regional languages. ---

metadata.title: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal
metadata.sectionTitle: 2. Features of the eCourts Services Mobile Application

content:
### 3. Alternative Citizen Channels

- **eCourts Services Web Portal:** [https://services.ecourts.gov.in](https://services.ecourts.gov.in) - **SMS Push/Pull Services:** Send SMS `ECORTR <CNR Number>` to 9766899899 to receive instant status updates. - **eCourts Suvidha Kiosks:** Touch-screen digital kiosks installed in judicial court complexes across India. - **eSewa Kendras:** Helpdesks established in court premises for bridging the digital divide, assisting non-tech-savvy citizens.

metadata.title: eCourts Services Mobile Application and Citizen Digital Portal

sectionTitle: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts
content:
### eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

> **Category:** Digital Court Procedures & Fees > **Source URL:** https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in > **Payment Portal:** https://pay.ecourts.gov.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts
metadata.sectionTitle: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### 1. What is eFiling?

eFiling (Version 3.0) is a digital platform designed by the eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India and NIC that enables advocates and party-in-person litigants to file cases electronically into Indian High Courts and District Courts 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. It completely eliminates physical paper filings, long queues at court registry filing counters, and delays in scrutiny. ---

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### Step 1: User Registration

1. Visit [https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in](https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in). 2. Register as an **Advocate** (requires Bar Council Enrollment Number, verification via OTP on registered mobile/email) or as a **Litigant / Party-in-Person**. 3. Set login credentials.

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### Step 2: Case Details Entry

1. Select the relevant State, District, and Court Establishment. 2. Choose Case Type (e.g., Civil Suit, Writ Petition, Criminal Appeal). 3. Enter details of Petitioner/Complainant and Respondent/Accused (names, addresses, contact details). 4. Specify the relevant legal Acts and Sections.

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### Step 3: Document Upload

1. Upload the petition/plaint, vakalatnama, affidavits, annexures, and supporting evidence. 2. Documents must be in searchable PDF format (OCR compliant). 3. Apply Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) or Aadhaar-based eSign.

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### Step 4: Verification and Token Generation

1. Complete digital verification. 2. An initial **eFiling Acknowledgement Number / Token** is generated for tracking Registry scrutiny. 3. Once approved by the Court Scrutiny Officer, a permanent Case Number and 16-digit CNR number are allocated. ---

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### 3. ePay: Online Court Fee Payment

- **Official Portal:** [https://pay.ecourts.gov.in](https://pay.ecourts.gov.in) - Integrated with State Treasury e-Gras portals and Bharatkosh. - Litigants and lawyers can pay: - Court Fees - Judicial Stamp Duties - Fines, Penalties, and Maintenance Deposits - Payment Methods: Net Banking, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, and UPI (BHIM, Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm). - Digital receipt with a unique transaction reference number is generated instantly to be attached to the eFiling docket. ---

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### 4. Official Links

- **eFiling System:** [https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in](https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in) - **ePay Portal:** [https://pay.ecourts.gov.in](https://pay.ecourts.gov.in)

metadata.title: eFiling and ePay Procedures in Indian Courts

content:
### Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

Category: ICT in Judiciary & Criminal Justice Source URL: https://doj.gov.in/inter-operable-criminal-justice-system/ Retrieval Date: 2026-11-11 Verification Status: Verified Official Government Data

metadata.title: Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

content:
### INTRODUCTION

The Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) is a national initiative spearheaded by the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, to integrate the key pillars of the criminal justice system in India.

metadata.title: Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

content:
### THE FIVE PILLARS OF ICJS

1. Police (Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems - CCTNS) 2. Courts (Case Information System - CIS under eCourts Mission Mode Project) 3. Prisons (e-Prisons application tracking inmate history, custody, and warrants) 4. Forensics (e-Forensics linking forensic laboratory analysis and reports) 5. Prosecution (e-Prosecution facilitating electronic chargesheets and status)

metadata.title: Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

content:
### CORE BENEFITS

- Real-time transmission of electronic FIRs and chargesheets directly from police stations to court dockets. - Instant execution of court summons and warrants through police digital networks. - Production of undertrial prisoners via high-definition video conferencing (VC), reducing security risks and transit expenses. - Accelerated justice delivery through seamless data exchange, eliminating missing case files and manual docket delays.

metadata.title: Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

content:
### PHASE II IMPLEMENTATION

Under Phase II of the ICJS project, the system has adopted One Data Once Entry principles with cloud infrastructure and dedicated APIs across all States and Union Territories.

metadata.title: Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)

sectionTitle: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings
content:
### Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings

> **Category:** Open Justice, Transparency & Virtual Hearings > **Source URL:** https://ecourts.gov.in > **Secondary Source:** https://main.sci.gov.in > **Retrieval Date:** 2026-11-08 > **Verification Status:** Verified Official Government Data ---

metadata.title: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings
metadata.sectionTitle: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings

content:
### 1. Background and Constitutional Foundation

In the landmark judgment *Swapnil Tripathi v. Supreme Court of India (2018)*, the Supreme Court held that live streaming of court proceedings is an extension of the **Open Court principle** enshrined under Article 21, Article 19(1)(a), and Article 145(4) of the Constitution of India. The eCommittee of the Supreme Court subsequently framed the model **Rules for Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings** to guide High Courts across India. ---

metadata.title: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings

sectionTitle: 2. Supreme Court of India Live Streaming
content:
### 2. Supreme Court of India Live Streaming

- Constitutional Bench hearings and matters of national significance are live streamed directly on the Supreme Court official YouTube channel and the dedicated Supreme Court web portal ([https://main.sci.gov.in](https://main.sci.gov.in)). - Full archived video recordings and audio transcripts (including AI-assisted real-time transcription powered by natural language models) are hosted for public educational access. ---

metadata.title: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings
metadata.sectionTitle: 2. Supreme Court of India Live Streaming

content:
### 3. High Courts Live Streaming Initiatives

Several High Courts have adopted formal rules and stream their court halls daily, including: - High Court of Gujarat (Pioneer in public streaming) - High Court of Karnataka - High Court of Madhya Pradesh - High Court of Orissa - High Court of Patna - High Court of Calcutta - High Court of Delhi Official streams are hosted on verified official High Court YouTube channels and institutional portals. ---

metadata.title: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings

content:
### 4. Exceptions and Restrictions (Matters NOT Streamed)

To protect privacy, national security, and vulnerable witnesses, the following matters are strictly exempted from live streaming: 1. Matrimonial and family disputes (divorce, custody, domestic violence). 2. Offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 3. Sexual assault and rape proceedings under Section 376 IPC / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. 4. Juvenile justice hearings. 5. In-camera proceedings and matters where the presiding judge directs confidentiality in the interest of justice. ---

metadata.title: Live Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings

sectionTitle: 1. What are Virtual Courts for Traffic Offenses?
content:
### 1. What are Virtual Courts for Traffic Offenses?

Virtual Courts are an initiative under the eCourts Project administered by the Department of Justice and the eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India. A Virtual Court is presided over by a judicial officer virtually, allowing petty offences-such as traffic violations and compoundable motor vehicle infractions-to be adjudicated completely online without requiring the presence of the citizen or advocate in physical courtrooms. ---

metadata.title: Traffic Violation Fine Payment and Virtual Courts (vcourts.gov.in)
metadata.sectionTitle: 1. What are Virtual Courts for Traffic Offenses?

sectionTitle: 2. Step-by-Step: How to Settle a Traffic Challan via Virtual Courts
content:
### 2. Step-by-Step: How to Settle a Traffic Challan via Virtual Courts

When an e-challan issued by the Traffic Police is transferred to a Virtual Court: 1. Visit the official Virtual Courts portal: [https://vcourts.gov.in](https://vcourts.gov.in). 2. Select your **State** and **Department / Court** (e.g., *Delhi - Notice Department* or *Maharashtra - Virtual Court*). 3. Search for your case using one of the following: - **Mobile Number** - **CNR Number** - **Challan Number** (from the traffic SMS/receipt) - **Vehicle Registration Number** - **Party Name** 4. View the violation summary, date, time, photographic evidence, and proposed fine determined by the Virtual Court Judge. 5. You are presented with two legal options: - **Plead Guilty:** Accept the offence and proposed fine. Proceed immediately to online payment via credit/debit card, net banking, or UPI. Upon payment, the case is officially marked **Disposed**, and an electronic receipt is issued. - **Contest / Do Not Plead Guilty:** If you dispute the violation or wish to challenge the fine, click *Contest*. The case is automatically transferred to the regular jurisdictional regular physical court for hearing. ---

metadata.title: Traffic Violation Fine Payment and Virtual Courts (vcourts.gov.in)
metadata.sectionTitle: 2. Step-by-Step: How to Settle a Traffic Challan via Virtual Courts

content:
### 3. Alternative: Direct Parivahan eChallan Settlement

Before a challan is transferred to court, it can often be paid directly on the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) portal: 1. Visit [https://echallan.parivahan.gov.in](https://echallan.parivahan.gov.in). 2. Click **Check Challan Status**. 3. Enter Challan Number, Vehicle Number, or Driving Licence Number. 4. Complete payment via payment gateway and download receipt. ---

sectionTitle: 1. What is the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG)?
content:
### 1. What is the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG)?

The National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) is a national data repository created under the eCourts Project that tracks judicial case status, pending cases, disposal rates, and institutional statistics across the entire Indian judiciary in real time. It is accessible to the public, policy makers, judges, and researchers, promoting unprecedented transparency in the administration of justice. In September 2023, the Supreme Court of India was also onboarded onto the NJDG open-access platform. ---
